title: Terengganu Half Marathon 2026 Review: Starting at Southeast Asia's First Drawbridge
meta_description: Terengganu Half Marathon 2026 review: October 31 at Kuala Terengganu Drawbridge -- the first drawbridge in Malaysia and Southeast Asia.
dek: Set for 31 October 2026, this JomRun-organised race starts at the Kuala Terengganu Drawbridge -- a 638-metre bascule bridge and the first of its kind built in Malaysia and Southeast Asia.
verdict: The Terengganu Half Marathon's genuine hook is its start point: the Kuala Terengganu Drawbridge, a 638-metre bascule bridge across the Terengganu River, completed in 2019 as the first drawbridge ever built in Malaysia or Southeast Asia. That's a rare piece of modern engineering to anchor a race around, distinct from the historic squares and malls hosting most other races in this research batch. Three distances (21.1K/10K/5K) with registration already open make this a straightforward East Coast Malaysia pick, especially for runners drawn to novel infrastructure landmarks.

sections.heading: A Race Anchored to a Genuine Engineering First
paragraphs: The race starts at the Kuala Terengganu Drawbridge, offering three distances: 21.1K, 10K and 5K. [1] The drawbridge is a bascule bridge crossing the Terengganu River, with a total length of 638 metres, width of 23 metres and height of 89.1 metres -- the first drawbridge ever built in Malaysia and all of Southeast Asia. [2]

sections.heading: Built as Part of a Regional Development Push
paragraphs: Construction began in August 2014 and finished in mid-2019, built by Zelan Construction Sdn Bhd at a cost of RM248 million, as part of the East Coast Economic Region (ECER) development initiative. [2] It's the fourth bridge crossing the river within Kuala Terengganu city, after the Sultan Mahmud, Manir and Pulau Sekati bridges -- but the only one with a lifting mechanism, making it a genuine local landmark rather than just infrastructure.

sections.heading: Standard JomRun Format
paragraphs: As with the KL Half Marathon and Tebrau City Half Marathon covered elsewhere in this research batch, this event is organised by JomRun -- giving it a familiar, tested race-day structure even in a less internationally known city. [1] Registration is currently open.

sections.heading: A Coastal East Malaysia Destination
paragraphs: Kuala Terengganu is the state capital of Terengganu on Malaysia's East Coast, a region less frequently visited by international runners than Kuala Lumpur or Penang -- giving this race a genuine off-the-beaten-path appeal for those willing to travel.

sections.heading: Should You Run It?
paragraphs: If starting a half marathon at a genuinely unique piece of modern engineering appeals -- Southeast Asia's first drawbridge -- the Terengganu Half Marathon on 31 October 2026 is a distinctive pick on Malaysia's East Coast. Registration is already open across all three distances.

faqs.question: Where does the Terengganu Half Marathon start?
faqs.answer: At the Kuala Terengganu Drawbridge, a 638-metre bascule bridge over the Terengganu River completed in 2019 -- the first drawbridge built in Malaysia and all of Southeast Asia. Three distances are offered: 21.1K, 10K and 5K. [1][2]

faqs.question: Who organises this race?
faqs.answer: JomRun, the same organiser behind the KL Half Marathon and Tebrau City Half Marathon covered elsewhere in this research batch. Registration is currently open for the 31 October 2026 race date. [1]

faqs.question: What makes the drawbridge significant?
faqs.answer: It was the first drawbridge ever built in Malaysia and Southeast Asia, completed in 2019 at a cost of RM248 million as part of the East Coast Economic Region development initiative -- a genuine engineering landmark for the race to start beside. [2]
